items.title: Andy Burnham sworn in as MP in hours after Starmer's resignation
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer has succumbed to pressure and resigned as prime minister of the UK, with likely successor Andy Burnham being sworn in as a new MP.

items.title: Meet the 'King of the North' set to become the UK's new PM
items.description: A popular mayor but a virtual unknown on the global stage, Andy Burnham is poised to become Sir Keir Starmer's successor. Here's what that could look like.

items.title: Perfect dupes of ABC articles are fuelling an industrial-scale scam
items.description: A $350 million scam is targeting Australians using AI-generated images of ABC journalists and politicians.

items.title: Photo gives clues to missing man's final hours before disappearance
items.description: A previously unreleased image answers one question in the case of missing Queensland man Jack McLennan, but many others remain.

items.title: Security agencies issue blunt 'act swiftly' warning on AI
items.description: The Five Eyes agencies warn leaders must "act swiftly" to address the imminent threat as AI increases the "speed, scale and sophistication of cyber threats".

items.title: Australians have record-low trust in the United States, new poll finds
items.description: The Lowy Institute's latest poll shows Australia's trust in the US has fallen to a record low.

items.title: Live: Wild weather, Mbappe screamers and a Messi milestone at the World Cup
items.description: Kylian Mbappe opens the scoring for France against Iraq after Lionel Messi becomes the top scorer in World Cup history. Follow live.

items.title: 'A little bit of whining' and other early takeaways from US–Iran talks
items.description: The US claims "great progress" has been made with Iran during the first substantial talks to take place under the new deal to pause the war, but there are already conflicting messages from Iran. Here's what we know about the results of the negotiations so far.

items.title: Live: Rush to pass CGT, negative gearing overhaul 'farcical': Pocock
items.description: An independent senator has labelled the government's rush to legislate its tax overhaul "farcical". Follow live.

items.title: The hidden dynamic that could undermine global stocks
items.description: As we plough on through the fourth consecutive year of global stock records and huge annual advances, it's not surprising that many pundits have begun to question just how much longer this boom can continue.

items.title: Inspired by volcanoes, this new technology could affect billions of people
items.description: Private companies want to reflect the Sun to cool the planet. But scientists fear the geoengineering technology could disrupt monsoon rains, on which a billion people depend.

items.title: Egg shortage unlikely as poultry industry braces for deadly bird flu
items.description: The poultry industry says it is concerned but prepared as the deadly H5 avian influenza variant reaches Australian shores for the first time.

items.title: Hantavirus cruise passengers released after 42 days in Perth quarantine
items.description: Six passengers from Australia and NZ linked to the deadly MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak have completed 42 days of quarantine in Perth and been cleared to return home.

items.title: Reflecting pool to be drained again weeks after multi-million-dollar renovation
items.description: The reflecting pool on Washington's National Mall will have to be drained again after algae and peeling paint appeared weeks after it was renovated.

items.title: This artist 'stole' the Rosetta Stone from the UK and took it home to Egypt
items.description: The Rosetta Stone changed the way we understood Ancient Egypt. It sits in the British Museum but this artist wanted to return it home. To pull it off he needed some legal advice, a digital scanner and the courage to take on the way we look at history.

items.title: You won't see Hugh Jackman the same after The Death of Robin Hood
items.description: Plus Toy Story 5 trots out the same old games, Australian horror scores another winner and Colony uses zombies to ring the warning bell about AI.

items.title: Quiz: Do you know a lychee from a rambutan? Name these fruits
items.description: Can you tell these tropical fruits apart? It's not as easy as you think.

items.title: $800k for mediation not spent prior to fatal stabbing
items.description: Mediation projects were a key part of the Barkly Regional Deal signed in 2019, but many locals are asking why the process seemed to have halted prior to the stabbing death of a young man amid unrest in Tennant Creek.

items.title: Logging company gives new answer to parliament over logs sent to Victoria
items.description: Sustainable Timber Tasmania has corrected the record after earlier stating that all logs from public native forests are processed in Tasmania.

items.title: Veterans paid extra $7m in abuse compensation after review
items.description: The Defence Force Ombudsman made the extra payments after a federal court case forced it to admit its reparation scheme didn't consider the ongoing impact of assaults.

items.title: Toll cap cut, new hospitals and schools: Inside NSW budget plans
items.description: NSW Treasurer Daniel Mookhey has tempered expectations of a return to surplus ahead of Tuesday's budget. Here's what has been promised so far.

items.title: Blues dealt fresh blow with Mitchell ruled out of Origin III
items.description: After a demoralising defeat to the Maroons, the Blues learn Latrell Mitchell will be unavailable for selection in the series-deciding State of Origin III.

items.title: Ex-Wimbledon champ handed four-year suspension for refusing doping test
items.description: Markéta Vondroušová, who lifted the Wimbledon trophy in 2023, is given a "significant ban" by the International Tennis Integrity Agency.

items.title: Nervous wait for farmers as bird flu investigation expands
items.description: Producers across an enormous stretch of southern WA are facing a tense few days, as authorities investigate more than 50 dead birds found along the state's southern coast.

items.title: Hanson says Ben Roberts-Smith should be welcome at War Memorial event
items.description: Federal parliament is set to adjourn early today so politicians can attend the official opening of a hall as part of the controversial $550 million extension of the War Memorial.
